newsitem.title: UK: Kazakh field "trouble spot" for British Gas.
newsitem.headline: Kazakh field "trouble spot" for British Gas.

text.p: The huge Karachaganak gas field in Kazakhstan has been a trouble spot for British Gas, chairman Richard Giordano told a news conference on Thursday.
"Karachaganak is unique. It's been a trouble spot for us as Kazakhstan has been for everyone. On the other hand, it is one huge reservoir of gas," he said.
British Gas and Italy's Agip SpA each hold a 42.5 percent interest in the field, with recoverable natural gas reserves of 1.33 trillion cubic metres.
The other partner is Russia's Gazprom with 15 percent.
"The strategy we've had with Agip is clearly respected as other companies have offered to take part or all of our position, so there is value there," said Giordano.
Giordano said British Gas was taking a "hard look at its portfolio", which is still skewed heavily towards the UK Continental Shelf.
But British Gas has reaped benefits in the first half of this year from developments in Trinidad, Thailand, Tunisia and the United States, he added.
